# Migration guide

## From 1.0.1 to 1.0.2

JSON Quality 1.0.2 keeps the CLI, SDK, configuration and schema contracts of 1.0.1.
No source or configuration migration is required.
Read [the release summary](support-and-release.md#changes-since-101) and [the changelog](../CHANGELOG.md#102) for the changes.

### Update the installation

Use the [exact-version installation command](consumer-guide.md#acquisition-and-public-exports) in the consumer guide.
Let npm update its lockfile, keep optional dependencies enabled, and commit both dependency declarations and the lockfile.
The matching Windows or Linux companion must have the same version as the core.
Run the project's existing JSON checks and integration tests after the update.

Node.js 22.13.0 remains the consumer minimum.
The native platforms remain Windows x64 and Linux x64 with glibc.
The [runtime compatibility policy](node-runtime-compatibility.md) lists qualified families and separates consumer requirements from contributor tooling.

### Keep repair selections explicit

For a repair limited to named files, put them after `--`:

```sh
npm exec -- json-quality format --dry-run --root . -- authored.json
npm exec -- json-quality format --write --root . -- authored.json
```

An unqualified filesystem format command selects all eligible writable files.
This is an existing contract clarified in the documentation, not a new behavior in 1.0.2.
Formatting preserves JSON meaning and exact number spellings; Unicode normalization remains a separate explicit operation with collision checks.

### Adapt release automation

Default release qualification now requires admitted CI evidence.
Use an ordinary same-repository merge after complete PR acceptance, inspect `REUSED`, and preserve the original manifest and proof bytes.
Missing or incompatible evidence stops; select `force-fresh` explicitly when complete requalification is intended.
Do not implement an automatic retry that silently starts another matrix.

For a promoted manifest, sign the version tag at `promotion.releaseCommit` and bind the owner review to the promoted manifest's digest.
The original package source and native production identities remain unchanged.
Writer reservations, private pending-stage observations, owner approvals and public-registry proof remain required.
Reserve each authorized rerun separately; a retained admission artifact keeps its original reservation and execution identity.
Use the exact signed staging checkpoint when original transport has expired, and retain the selected predecessor when exporting renewed history.
An upload-only failure after complete native staging requests can supply a separately admitted core continuation; it never authorizes restaging the native packages.
For pilot retirement, observe an acknowledged prefix without repeating removals.
Settle an exact rejected request from native proof and record a fresh owner decision before attempting the remaining aliases.
See [release operations](release-operations.md) for the complete sequence and [failure recovery](release-operations.md#failure-recovery-and-evidence) before repeating any interrupted action.
